samples.summary: Quadratic `snapFreezePastMerges` runs synchronously on an attacker-controlled, uncapped merge map (authenticated DoS of the whole backend process)
samples.evidence: `snapFreezePastMerges` (merging.ts:217) re-scans ALL merge entries on every pass and advances the boundary by at most one block per pass, so its cost is O(passes x entries). Both the number of entries and their iteration order are attacker-controlled: `parseMerges` (backend/src/yorkie/worksheet-settings.ts:107-157) caps each span's covered cells (MaxMergedCells=100000) but places NO cap on how MANY entries the map may hold, and object key order is insertion order for non-numeric keys like "A1". Attack: with any API key that has write scope on one document, (1) `PUT .../tabs/:tabId/merges` with N chained 2-row blocks emitted in DESCENDING anchor order (A_N:[N,N+1], ..., A1:[1,2]) — accepted, since the tab's freeze is 0 so `assertMergesClearOfFreeze` returns early (worksheet.controller.ts:189); (2) `PUT .../tabs/:tabId/freeze` with `{rows:1}` — worksheet.controller.ts:112 now calls `snapFreezePastMerges` INSIDE the synchronous `doc.update` callback, which advances rows by exactly one per full pass, giving N^2 `parseRef`/`toMergeRange` iterations with no yield. The 25MB JSON body limit (backend/src/main.ts:20) admits several hundred thousand entries; even N=20k is ~4e8 iterations of blocked event loop per request, and N=200k is ~4e10 — the Node process (shared by every tenant) stops serving. The default throttle of 120 req/min is more than enough to keep it wedged. The same loop is also newly on the engine's hot path — `Sheet.shiftCells` (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:1418) runs it on EVERY row/column insert or delete — so a merge map planted through the API also freezes every collaborator's browser on the next structural edit. Suggested fix: cap the number of merge entries in `parseMerges`, and/or make the snap single-pass by folding entries into a max over crossing blocks instead of restarting the scan.

samples.summary: Freeze snap result is stored without re-clamping to the grid bounds `parseFreeze` enforces as a DoS guard
samples.evidence: `parseFreeze` bounds rows/cols to MaxRows=1e6 / MaxColumns=18278 precisely because, per its own comment (backend/src/yorkie/worksheet-settings.ts:46-53), "the frozen quadrants render every frozen row and column without viewport clipping, so an out-of-grid freeze allocates per frame and the UI never paints — which also means the user cannot reach the freeze menu to undo it." worksheet.controller.ts:112-119 now writes `snapped.frozenRows/frozenCols` — values derived from the stored merge map's block extents (`range[1].r`, merging.ts:222/226), not from the validated body — straight into the document with no re-clamp. Any merge written by a path that does not go through `parseMerges` (the collaborative Yorkie client, or `xlsx-importer.ts:258` which copies merge extents straight out of an uploaded workbook) can therefore make a `PUT freeze {rows:1}` store a frozen boundary past the validated ceiling, turning a legal request into a persistent render-DoS for every collaborator on that tab. I could not confirm a concrete writer that exceeds 1e6 rows, hence low confidence, but the clamp that used to be guaranteed by `parseFreeze` is no longer applied to what is actually stored. Clamp `snapped` to MaxRows/MaxColumns (or refuse) before assigning.

samples.summary: `PUT freeze` now parses stored merge keys with `parseRef`, which throws a raw Error — a malformed stored key turns a valid request into a 500
samples.evidence: `parseRef` throws a bare `Error('Invalid Reference')` on any key it cannot parse (packages/sheets/src/model/core/coordinates.ts:351). Before this change `PUT .../freeze` never read `ws.merges`; now worksheet.controller.ts:112 feeds every stored merge key into `snapFreezePastMerges` -> `parseRef` (merging.ts:220) inside `doc.update`, with no try/catch. A merge key written by any writer that bypasses `parseMerges` (a client talking to Yorkie directly, or a future importer) becomes a poison pill that makes the freeze endpoint return 500 (leaking a stack through Nest's default filter in non-production configs) for every caller until the key is removed. The same exposure exists for the new `assertMoveKeepsMergesOffFreeze` path (worksheet-structure.controller.ts:187). Wrapping the key parse and skipping/400-ing on unparseable keys would keep the endpoint available.

verdict.reason: Every claimed element verified in the tree. merging.ts:217-230 is a restart-on-change loop that re-scans all materialized entries per pass and advances the freeze boundary by at most one crossing block per pass, giving O(passes x entries) synchronous parseRef/toMergeRange work with no yield. parseMerges (worksheet-settings.ts:107-157) validates each key and caps rs*cs at MaxMergedCells (line 148) but places NO cap on the NUMBER of entries in the map, and permits overlapping/chained spans. The plant step is accepted because assertMergesClearOfFreeze (worksheet.controller.ts:189) returns early when the tab's freeze is 0, so a chain of 2-row blocks is stored verbatim (line 249). The trigger, snapFreezePastMerges, is invoked inside the synchronous doc.update callback of PUT freeze (worksheet.controller.ts:112-116), so the quadratic scan blocks the event loop of the shared multi-tenant Node process for the duration of the request. Amplifiers confirmed: 25MB JSON body limit (main.ts:20) admits hundreds of thousands of entries, and the default 120 req/min throttle (app.module.ts:102) is far more than needed to keep the process wedged. The same loop is also on the engine hot path at sheet.ts:1418 (every row/column insert or delete), so a planted map hangs collaborators' clients too. No guard elsewhere bounds merge-map cardinality or the snap's work; MaxMergedCells bounds only a single span's area. Attacker-controlled, unbounded input driving super-linear synchronous work with cross-tenant availability impact is an input-validation/resource-exhaustion vulnerability within the security lane, not a general correctness bug, so no refutation ground applies.

mergedFrom.summary: `PUT freeze` now parses stored merge keys with `parseRef`, which throws a raw Error — a malformed stored key turns a valid request into a 500
mergedFrom.evidence: `parseRef` throws a bare `Error('Invalid Reference')` on any key it cannot parse (packages/sheets/src/model/core/coordinates.ts:351). Before this change `PUT .../freeze` never read `ws.merges`; now worksheet.controller.ts:112 feeds every stored merge key into `snapFreezePastMerges` -> `parseRef` (merging.ts:220) inside `doc.update`, with no try/catch. verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described. worksheet.controller.ts:112-119 assigns snapFreezePastMerges' output straight into ws.frozenRows/frozenCols with no re-clamp. parseFreeze (worksheet-settings.ts:54-60, bounds at 10-11) only validates the *input* rows/cols against MaxRows=1e6 / MaxColumns=18278, and its own comment (46-53) says that bound exists because frozen quadrants render without viewport clipping — i.e. it is an availability guard. snapFreezePastMerges (merging.ts:207-233) raises rows/cols to range[1].r / range[1].c (lines 222, 226) taken from the stored merge map, with no ceiling. Contrary to the reviewer's own stated uncertainty, a concrete out-of-bounds writer does exist: xlsx-importer.ts:240-263 writes worksheet.merges[...] = {rs, cs} computed from an attacker-supplied mergeCell ref through safeParseRef (147-153), which wraps parseRef; parseRef (coordinates.ts:337-367) applies no upper bound on row/col, so an XLSX merge ref like A1:XFD1048576 stores rs=1048576 > MaxRows. A legal PUT freeze {rows:1} then snaps to and persists that value. No downstream clamp exists: getFreeze (worksheet.controller.ts:83), memory.ts:214 and worksheet-shape-migration.ts:449 all pass the value through verbatim. No refutation ground applies (not not-present, not already-guarded). Confidence is low only because the impact is availability/DoS rather than a classic authz/secret/injection vector, which is a reason to keep the finding rather than drop it.
